title: Binary, constant relative volatility 2.5, total condenser
purpose: (a) A constant-alpha binary where the rigorous column must equal McCabe-Thiele's construction exactly, and where the shortcut's equations can be checked by hand.
method_choice: constant-alpha model system (no method to choose)

thermo.note: A model system, not a real mixture: K_i = alpha_i p(T) / P with the reference vapour pressure p(T) above (made up; it only fixes the temperatures), liquid enthalpy 0 and vapour enthalpy equal to the latent heat for every component, so the energy balances give constant molar overflow exactly. docs/METHOD_SELECTION.md does not apply: there is no real mixture to choose a method for.

behaviour: the profile equals McCabe-Thiele's stage-by-stage construction from x_D with the same flows (fixture: checks.mccabe_thiele)
constant molar overflow: L = R D above the feed, L + qF below; V = (R + 1) D on every stage below the condenser
the temperature rises from the top to the bottom
at a very large reflux ratio the separation tends to Fenske's alpha^(N - 1) (fixture: checks.total_reflux)
expected.branch: One solution expected (constant relative volatility with constant molar overflow and specifications of reflux ratio and a product flow): the reference's solution is the one to match.

engine_against_reference.why: Proposal 0015, Engineering basis: flows within 1e-6 relative of the independent MESH solution. Both solve the same equations to residuals of 1e-8 or less, so the difference is the solvers' convergence only.

balances_on_every_stage.why: Proposal 0015: every stage's balances closed to 1e-8. Material: |residual| / F; energy: |residual| / (F x 10 kJ/mol); summation and equilibrium are mole fractions.
